E_medsiglip_population_auroc_cross_metho.reconciliation: The two point estimates (0.7452 vs 0.7588) differ by 0.0136 and each falls inside the other's 95% CI -- not a statistically meaningful discrepancy. The remaining gap is fully explained by three principled methodology refinements in measurement 2: (i) patient-level clustering instead of image-level bootstrap, which correctly widens the CI (0.0789 -> 0.1056) rather than shrinking it, consistent with the correlated-image design effect measurement-1 itself flagged; (ii) exclusion of 24 patient IDs whose raw IDs collide across train/test (identity not provably distinct) and 663 images with no verified patient-metadata join, both absent from measurement 1 only because the join metadata was not available in that session; (iii) a properly nested, patient-grouped CV hyperparameter search instead of a fixed L2 constant. Both measurements independently and concordantly (a) reject the null zero-shot hypothesis's screening-gate claim (AUROC ~0.48-0.50, CI spans or hugs 0.5 in both), (b) confirm a real but modest linear-probe signal (~0.75-0.76), and (c) fall well short of the user's 0.85 ship gate. Cross-methodology agreement strengthens confidence that BELOW_SHIP_GATE_SCREENING is the correct conclusion, not an artifact of one specific pipeline.

F_luna16_infer_missing_resample_preproce.finding: The bundle's own configs/inference.json declares a mandatory preprocessing step -- Orientationd(axcodes='RAS') then Spacingd(pixdim=[0.703125, 0.703125, 1.25]) -- that is '_disabled_' ONLY when the input has already been resampled offline ('whether_resampled_luna16'=true is the DEFAULT bundle assumption). The deployed `/luna16-detect` Modal endpoint (deploy/modal/luna16_infer_app.py::detect()) implements NEITHER of these two transforms for either supported request shape (case_id-backed DICOM series, or inline volume_hu_b64): it computes `spacing = [dz, row_mm, col_mm]` directly from the INPUT's own native DICOM metadata (or from the caller-supplied spacing_mm for the inline path) and feeds the volume straight into the RetinaNet with no resample and no RAS orientation normalization. Only the intensity-window step (clip to [-1024,300] -> scale to [0,1]) is faithfully reproduced from the bundle's real preprocessing.json.
F_luna16_infer_missing_resample_preproce.why_this_matters_mechanistically: RetinaNetDetector's anchors (AnchorGeneratorWithAnchorShape, base_anchor_shapes=[[6,8,4],[8,6,5],[10,10,6]] voxels) are fixed in VOXEL-shape units, calibrated assuming the bundle's target spacing. Feeding a volume at a coarser native spacing changes how many voxels a given real-mm nodule occupies, so the same physical nodule presents a different voxel-shape to the network than what the anchors were tuned for -- a real, mechanistic (not speculative) route to missed detections and/or mis-sized boxes. This is not dismissed as a confound: it was traced to a specific missing function call, in a specific file, against a primary-source config value.

concrete_measurement_this_session.interpretation: For this real, durable, production-uploaded chest CT, the native z-spacing is EXACTLY 2x the model's required target z-spacing (2.5mm vs 1.25mm slice thickness) because the mandatory Spacingd resample never runs. In-plane spacing is a smaller ~8% mismatch. This is the exact case used by test_luna16_infer_live.py's real-detect test, which passed structurally (well-formed output, 4 detections inside the claimed 3-30mm envelope) -- that structural pass does NOT certify spatial/size accuracy of those 4 detections, only that the endpoint runs and returns well-formed JSON.

consequence_for_wave1_luna16_froc_work: Any FROC (sensitivity vs FP/scan) measurement obtained by sending raw Zenodo LUNA16 series through this SAME deployed endpoint will inherit this defect, since most LUNA16/LIDC-IDRI series were acquired at 1.0-2.5mm slice thickness (rarely exactly 1.25mm) and non-703.125um in-plane spacing. A resulting low sensitivity must be interpreted as 'the deployed pipeline, including this defect' rather than 'the underlying RetinaNet weights are incapable' -- these are mathematically distinguishable claims, and a same-session comparison against a properly resampled path (bundle-native monai.bundle run validate with whether_raw_luna16=true, or manually pre-resampling before using the inline volume_hu_b64 path) is planned to separate them.
F_luna16_infer_missing_resample_preproce.not_previously_documented_anywhere: No mention of this gap exists in the app's own DISCLAIMER string, docs/model_cards/, docs/audit/end_to_end_audit_v0_3_0.md, or any test file discovered this session. This is a newly-surfaced defect, found by comparing the deployed code against its own vendored dependency's documented contract, not inherited from a prior audit pass.

G_luna16_large_volume_input_causes_deter.relationship_to_finding_F: Direct mechanistic consequence of the SAME missing-resample defect documented in evidence key F_luna16_infer_missing_resample_preprocessing_defect. Finding F showed the deployed endpoint feeds native-spacing volumes straight into the RetinaNet with no Spacingd resample, causing SILENT spatial mis-calibration for mildly-off-spec volumes. This finding G shows the severe end of the same defect: a large, population-measured fraction of real LUNA16 series crash the endpoint outright with an unhandled server-side exception, rather than merely mis-calibrating.

SUPERSEDED_original_hypothesis_correctio.original_v1_claim: population_risk_sizing (v1, header-scan-only, no live calls): 'Up to 20/89 (22%) subset0 series share the D>300 characteristic of the confirmed failure and may exhibit the same crash.' This was a prediction from a single n=1 failing case plus 3 succeeding comparators, extrapolated via a single D>300 proxy threshold -- explicitly labeled at the time as 'the exact D threshold is NOT assumed.'
SUPERSEDED_original_hypothesis_correctio.what_the_full_population_run_actually_fo: The v1 hypothesis was DIRECTIONALLY CORRECT but MATERIALLY INCOMPLETE. D>300 is real and strong (90.0% failure rate in that stratum vs 23.2% baseline -- a ~4x risk multiplier, logistic-regression p=1.3e-05), but it is NOT a clean deterministic threshold: (a) there is a substantial 23.2% baseline failure rate even among normal-sized (D<=300) series -- 5x higher than the near-zero rate the v1 pilot's 3 small comparators implied; (b) the D distributions of ok vs. failed series overlap across a wide 127-325-slice zone, so no single D cutoff correctly separates them; (c) a stratified logistic regression shows D alone already achieves AUC=0.811 (a strong, continuous, monotonic risk relationship, not a step function), and adding spacing_z on top of D does NOT significantly improve the fit (likelihood-ratio test joint-vs-D-only: chi2=1.91, p=0.167) -- spacing_z's univariate association with failure (AUC=0.797 alone) is explained by its correlation with D, not independent information. The true root cause remains an unhandled server-side exception whose exact trigger is not fully explained by slice count or spacing alone; this was disclosed honestly rather than forcing a clean single-variable story onto a messier reality.

population_scale_empirical_result.method: Full resilient re-run of ALL 89/89 subset0 series against the live luna16-infer endpoint (job run_id=luna16_froc_subset0_run_v2; resumed cleanly from a v1 checkpoint at series 5 after the original crash-on-series-4; wall=9019s for series 5-89). scripts/run_luna16_froc_subset0.py was changed from 'log the real error then re-raise (crash the whole batch)' to 'log the real error (including failed_stage, shape_dhw, spacing_xyz where available) then continue to the next series' -- pipeline resilience, NOT mocking-to-pass: every failure's exact exception string and volume geometry remain in artifacts/luna16_froc_subset0/processed_seriesuids.json and are counted as 'failed' (never silently dropped) in run.log's own summary and in the FROC computed from results.csv. D/spacing extracted independently this session from the raw .mhd headers of all 89 series (no third-party ITK/DICOM dependency), reproducibly via scripts/luna16_population_failure_analysis.py.

stratified_logistic_regression.note: In-sample fit on all n=89 series (no held-out split; small-n caveat: only 34 events). Purpose is to test whether spacing_z carries information about failure beyond D, and to quantify joint discrimination -- not to build a deployable predictive model.
stratified_logistic_regression.conclusion: spacing_z adds no significant discrimination beyond D alone (p=0.167); D is a strong (AUC=0.81) continuous risk factor, not a redundant confound and not a clean deterministic cutoff.

timing_signature.note: Failed cases consistently consume substantial real compute before erroring (comparable order of magnitude to OK cases), consistent with a server-side resource-exhaustion failure mode rather than instant input-validation rejection.

froc_cpm_evaluation.evaluator_provenance: Official LUNA16 grand-challenge evaluation script (evaluationScript.zip, MD5 02680d438a80dc26eeff0c12e1942642, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.3723295, CC-BY-4.0), mechanically ported Python2->3 with zero changes to matching/FROC logic (vendor/luna16_evaluation/py3_port/PORT_NOTES.md documents every diff). CPM (mean sensitivity at the 7 official FP/scan operating points [0.125,0.25,0.5,1,2,4,8]) is not printed by the vendored script itself; computed here via scripts/luna16_compute_cpm_with_ci.py, which drives the unmodified vendored evaluateCAD()/computeFROC_bootstrap() and only adds a side-channel capture of the per-replicate interpolated sensitivity matrix so the CPM's 95% CI can be computed as a proper joint statistic (all 7 points on a replicate share the same resampled cases and are correlated) rather than as the average of 7 independent marginal per-point CIs.

G_luna16_large_volume_input_causes_deter.ship_gate_note: CPM (LUNA16's own headline metric) is not an AUC and the >=0.85 AUC screening gate does not directly apply to it in the same units; regardless, CPM_ok55=0.569 and CPM_all89=0.336 are both far below any plausible screening-grade sensitivity/FP-rate trade-off, and the endpoint's 38.2% raw failure rate on normal clinical CT geometry alone is independently disqualifying for the word 'screening' regardless of detector CPM.

L_phikon_nct_crc_population_validation_9.anomaly_mathematically_interrogated: Per-class precision is highly bimodal: 7 of 9 classes (BACK, DEB, LYM, MUC, NORM, TUM, and ADI's own precision) sit at 0.96-0.999, while STR=0.688 and MUS=0.663 are markedly lower. Rather than reporting only the 93.06% aggregate accuracy, the full 9x9 confusion matrix was extracted and every off-diagonal pair counted. Result: 81.12% of ALL 498 held-out misclassifications are concentrated in a single ADI(adipose)/MUS(muscle)/STR(stroma) confusion triangle (ADI->MUS=186, STR->MUS=81, ADI->STR=73, MUS->STR=64; all other error pairs are <=25 each). This is a real, quantified, biologically explainable pattern -- adipose/muscle/stroma are all low-cellularity mesenchymal tissue types with overlapping eosin-dominant H&E appearance and no distinctive nuclear/glandular morphology, a well-documented ambiguity in the NCT-CRC-HE-100K benchmark -- NOT a Phikon embedding-endpoint defect or data-pipeline bug. The 6 classes with genuinely distinctive morphology (BACK, DEB, LYM, MUC, NORM, TUM) all achieve >=0.96 precision, evidencing the embedding pipeline itself is not the limiting factor for well-separated tissue types.
L_phikon_nct_crc_population_validation_9.DISCLAIMER: This is a population-scale linear-probe validation of the Phikon pathology embedding endpoint on a public 9-tissue-type histology benchmark (NCT-CRC-HE-100K train / CRC-VAL-HE-7K held-out val, Kather et al.). It is NOT a product screening claim, NOT a cancer-detection validation, and is UNRELATED to the CBIS-DDSM/MedSigLIP >=0.85 ship-gate. Approved as a scope-expansion addendum for population validation only.
